newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish teenagers to appeal in police torture case.
newsitem.headline: Turkish teenagers to appeal in police torture case.

text.p: Ten Turks, many of them teenage students, are to appeal against jail sentences of up to twelve-and-a half years given to them for leftist activities in a case marked by police torture accusations, supporters said on Friday.

"We will apply to the appeals court. If we do not get a result we will go to the European Court of Human Rights but we would prefer to clean up this torture disgrace inside the domestic legal system," said social democrat MP Sabri Ergul.
A court in the western town of Manisa on Thursday sentenced the ten for membership of a leftist urban guerrilla group.

Four 19-year-old high school pupils received two-and-a half years in jail. A female university student aged 20 was given more than three years and five others, including a 30-year-old teacher accused of being the ringleader, were sentenced to twelve-and-a half years.
"There is no evidence expect the kids' own confessions, which were taken under torture," Manisa deputy Ergul told Reuters.

Ergul is the youngsters' lawyer in a case they brought against ten policemen who allegedly tortured them after rounding them up randomly on charges of belonging to the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party - Front (DHKP-C) group.
The youths say police tortured them for ten days, stripping them naked, anally raping them with batons, giving them electric shocks and hosing them with pressurised water.
The mass-circulation Hurriyet daily on Thursday pointed to the swift treatment given to the Manisa case as opposed to the authorities' slow pace in investigating a recent security scandal.
"Here's the gang," the paper said in a sarcastic banner headline under a photograph of two female teenagers in tears during the Manisa trial.

The headline was a reference to a report by an investigative body controlled by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan which said last week that it could find no evidence of organised crime gangs within the state system.

The media says leading officials were deeply involved in heroin smuggling, political murders, forgery and extortion. Legal authorities are studying the possibility of lifting the parliamentary immunity of two government MPs linked to the scandal.
"The state, unable to show its teeth against gangs and the Mafia, takes it out on schoolchildren," Hurriyet said.
